expected_mechanism: Switch to LQR will occur (error grows to ~0.6 m); recovery hinges on whether the 0.04 rad bias can be corrected before lateral acceleration exceeds the 4.41 * 0.8 limit

Larger on-time increases mean bias above 0.0749 rad (benchmark). Faster speed raises e_y at switch. The boundary lies where the accumulated error just crosses the supervisor trigger and LQR cannot settle within lane bounds
Drift rate lower than the 0.0492 failed case; at 25 km/h with 0.6 friction the steady-state error e_y = rate/|kappa| may hover near the 0.6 m trigger. A small speed or friction increase tips recovery

Shorter duration than the 0.672 recovered case; magnitude 0.6 vs 0.764. At 25 km/h the lateral acceleration demand is lower; boundary where the clipped LQR rate limit (90 deg/s) can no longer prevent the error from growing past 0.6 m during the switch delay
increased bias magnitude and reduced tyre grip push safety margin toward zero while MPC still triggers LQR switch via steer_rate_exceeded
stronger constant bias and earlier onset cause tracking error to reach divergence threshold, enabling first LQR switch
two-tick output delay plus later onset offset accumulates lateral error past supervisor trigger, achieving switch with modest recovery margin
